blocks.content: Economic reforms refer to the changes introduced by the government to improve the efficiency and competitiveness of the economy. In India, major economic reforms were introduced in 1991 to overcome the severe economic crisis and promote economic growth.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 1991 Economic Reforms were launched under Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
Liberalization dismantled the 'License Raj', deregulating most industrial sectors and easing business operations.
Privatization reduced the state's direct ownership in public sector undertakings (PSUs) through strategic disinvestment.
Globalization integrated the Indian economy with the global market by relaxing FDI norms and reducing trade tariffs.
The reforms were triggered by a severe Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis and depleting foreign exchange reserves in 1991.

blocks.content: • In 1991, India faced a severe economic crisis.
• Foreign exchange reserves were very low.
• The government introduced economic reforms to stabilize the economy.
• The reforms aimed to promote liberalization, privatization and globalization.
• Liberalization refers to the removal of government restrictions on economic activities.
• It reduces government control over industries.
• Privatization means transferring ownership of public sector enterprises to private sector.
The New Economic Policy of 1991 launched deep structural reforms through Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization.
• It reduces the financial burden on the government.
• Globalization refers to the integration of the Indian economy with the world economy.
• It promotes international trade and investment.
• It allows foreign companies to invest in India.

rows: Liberalized FDI under automatic and government routes
High import tariffs and quantitative restrictions
Reduced tariffs and integration with world trade
Dominant presence reserved for state enterprise
Increased private participation and PSU disinvestment

items: Economic Reforms of 1991 are frequently referred to as the Rao-Manmohan Model in competitive examinations.
The immediate cause of the 1991 LPG reforms was the Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis where foreign exchange reserves dropped to cover barely two weeks of imports.
Abolition of Industrial Licensing for most industries except a few strategic sectors was a key milestone of Liberalization.

blocks.content: • Economic reforms in India started in 1991.
• The reforms are based on LPG policy.
• LPG stands for Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization.
